campaign: Matched Qwen3-8B benchmark coverage · completed scores and continuing native evaluations

benchmarks.label: Full scores available · more native models running
benchmarks.summary: Teacher, quantized controls, eight-cell hybrid and the 8-FFN/50%-value native model have complete scores.
items: Full augmented EvalPlus tests: HumanEval+ 164 problems; MBPP+ 378 problems.
All six native BF16 endpoints remain scheduled; completed results, including losses, are appended.
Matched local greedy nonthinking H100 protocol; not exact Prism reproduction.

Against PrismML’s own reported scores: teacher −1.8, ternary Bonsai −4.8, 1-bit Bonsai −2.5. The ternary Bonsai’s gap exceeds our 3-point comparability test, so these are local measurements, not PrismML reproductions; new results are appended with the gaps stated.

benchmarks.label: Prompting-mode evaluation being recorded
benchmarks.summary: Our first BFCL run used function-calling mode, which is not PrismML’s protocol. Those scores now have their own chart, “BFCL v3 · function-calling mode”; this chart keeps PrismML-comparable prompting-mode scores.
items: PrismML Appendix B.5.2: prompting mode (tools in the system prompt, is_fc_model=false, underscore_to_dot=false); macro-average of the 13 single-turn subsets.
Withdrawn on 29 Sep 2026: function-calling scores published earlier that day under this name as a sample-weighted accuracy.
In function-calling mode our local 1-bit and ternary Bonsai scored 10.9 and 3.9 points above PrismML’s reported BFCL (macro-average); the teacher was 0.7 below.

benchmarks.label: Not PrismML’s protocol
benchmarks.summary: BFCL v3 with tools passed through the chat template (function-calling mode). Compare models only within this chart, never with PrismML’s BFCL v3 scores.
items: 3,641 cases across the 13 single-turn subsets; macro-average of the subset accuracies.
EvalScope 1.4.2, is_fc_model=true, underscore_to_dot=true, greedy nonthinking, 4,096-token cap; frozen H100 generations.
Teacher 80.3 here; ternary Bonsai 77.8; 1-bit Bonsai 76.6.
